_comment: Where this project's Conan packages come from. Read this before adding a dependency.
remote -- the normal case. A package a Conan remote carries is declared once, by version, in
conandata.yml; there is nothing to keep here.
local  -- a package no remote carries. Keep the CCI-shaped recipe under local-packages/ and
describe it here; `python3 .github/project/package_sources.py` exports it into the
cache and builds it for the configuration that asks for it.
A recipe rather than a built artifact is the whole point: it builds from source per platform,
so Windows, macOS and every cross profile get their own package. A committed binary would be
bound to one configuration and either skipped or, worse, linked anyway on a foreign host.
An absent local recipe is not an error: the leg that needs it says so and is skipped, which
is what lets a clean clone build.
Compilers and emulators are declared in toolchains.json:tool_sources -- they are governed by the toolchain rules, not by the package rules.

packages.name: cmsis-nn
packages.if_absent: the leg that enables compile_options.with_cmsis_nn is skipped and says which recipe it wanted; every other leg is unaffected
